items.title: Build the retention programme: milestones, digests, dormancy and its kill criterion
items.outcome: Debt milestones, a weekly or monthly progress digest and a dormancy re-engagement path are delivered under consent-aware frequency caps, and the whole programme carries a written threshold at which it is switched off rather than tuned forever.
items.context: Retention is the risk most likely to kill this product and the one with the least owned work. The debt-first wedge is the answer on paper; nothing implements the loop that makes a user come back. The danger in building it is the opposite failure: a nagging app that a user mutes and then uninstalls. That is why this ticket carries a kill criterion rather than only a set of messages - a retention programme with no threshold for stopping becomes permanent regardless of whether it works.
scope: Debt milestone detection and celebration: first payment, a percentage retired, a debt closed, and the payoff date moving earlier
Weekly or monthly progress digest with the user's chosen cadence, including an off option
Frequency caps across all retention classes, evaluated together rather than per message
Consent awareness: a class the user has not enabled is never sent, and the digest cadence is a user choice rather than a default the user must discover
Dormancy detection and a bounded re-engagement sequence with a hard stop
In-app equivalents so the loop still works for a user who denied notification permission
A written kill and reconsider threshold: the metric, the measurement window, the value at which the programme is switched off, and who decides
Holdout group so the effect of the programme is measured rather than assumed
acceptance_criteria: Every retention message class is off unless the user has enabled it or the class is one the user chose a cadence for; no class defaults to on without a recorded choice
The combined frequency cap is enforced across classes, proven by a test that generates several eligible messages in one window and asserts only the capped number is sent
A dormancy sequence stops after the published number of attempts and never restarts without a new qualifying event, proven by a test
A user who denied notification permission still receives milestone and digest content in-app, so the loop is not conditional on a permission
The kill criterion is recorded as a numeric threshold on a named metric over a named window, with the owner who decides and the action taken if it is breached
A holdout group exists and the reported effect of the programme is the difference against it, not the absolute behaviour of messaged users
Unsubscribing from a retention class takes effect immediately and is never overridden by another class's schedule
No retention message contains a monetary amount, a merchant name or another user's identity, consistent with the T-NOT-01 payload allowlist
contracts_schema: Consumes the messaging preference and delivery contract from T-CON-11; retention defines message classes within that vocabulary and adds no delivery mechanism of its own
security_privacy: Retention content is derived on the device or from already-authorised server data; no new data collection is introduced to support it
The holdout assignment is stable and recorded, and is never used for any purpose other than measuring this programme
observability: Per-class send, open, mute and unsubscribe rates, plus the retention metric named in the kill criterion, are all recorded against the holdout
A rising mute or uninstall rate following a retention send raises an alert rather than waiting for the next review
tests: Combined frequency cap test across classes
Payload allowlist conformance test for every retention template
rollout_rollback: One class at a time, starting with the milestone that follows a user action the user just took, measured against the holdout before the next class is enabled
Rollback is disabling a class, which takes effect at send time; the kill criterion makes switching the whole programme off a planned outcome rather than an admission of failure
non_goals: Delivery machinery, which T-NOT-01 and T-NOT-02 own
Gamification: streaks, points, badges and leaderboards are deliberately not part of this programme
Any message that is not triggered by the user's own financial activity or their chosen cadence
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo android. Owns milestone detection, digest composition, cadence and the in-app equivalents. Delivery, preferences and suppression belong to T-NOT-01; the funnel instrumentation it measures against belongs to android#6.
definition_of_done: Merged only after a current-head core-reviewer attestation from a separate qualified reviewer-agent session
Every acceptance criterion demonstrated by a named automated test or attached evidence
Tests listed in this ticket run in CI, and their check names and the local commands that reproduce them are recorded for T-SCA-INF-01
Observability, rollout and rollback notes recorded on the ticket before merge
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges
